Instrument.name: Mid-Infrared Array Camera (MIRAC)
Instrument.description: The Mid-Infrared Array Camera (MIRAC) was an instrument that a Hughes Aircraft Co. 20 X 64 pixel arsenic-doped silicon impurity band conduction hybrid array with a capacitance transimpedance amplifier readout (CRC 444A) operated at 10 K in a liquid-helium-cooled cryostat. The operating wavelength of MIRAC was 2 to 26 microns. Using 20 parallel readout lines and frame rate of 10 KHz, the array exhibited low noise and good linearity at high background flux, which was essential for 10 and 20 micron ground-based observing conditions. Peak efficiency of 0.42 at 22 micron, and a well size of 120,000 electrons. MIRAC operated on Steward Observatory 2.3-meter and the IRTF 3.0-meter telescopes for observing a variety of objects including infrared-luminous galaxies, planetary nebulae, star forming regions, young stellar objects, and Solar System objects. The NEFD of the MIRAC on the IRTF at 11.7 micron is 0.1 Jy/arcsec^2 in one second of integration on-source, four seconds of total time, including nodding and chopping off-source.
